newsitem.title: CANADA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-CANADIENS NAME ALAIN VIGNEAULT NEW HEAD COACH.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-CANADIENS NAME ALAIN VIGNEAULT NEW HEAD COACH.

text.p: The Montreal Canadiens on Monday named Alain Vigneault their new head coach and hired former Calgary Flames coach Dave King as his top assistant.
Canadiens general manager Rejean Houle announced that former junior league head coach Vigneault had signed a three-year contract for the most pressure-packed post in the National Hockey League.
Vigneault said he felt he could handle the intense media scrutiny and exceedingly high expectations of Montreal fans that come with the job.
"I've always had good relationships with the press," he said at Monday's news conference. "If we win, the fans are going to be happy."
Vigneault replaces Mario Tremblay, who resigned April 30 after the team was eliminated in the first round of the playoffs.

The 36-year-old Vigneault spent the last 1 1/2 seasons with the Beauport Harfangs of the Quebec Major Junior Hockey League. He also coached the Hull Olympiques in that league and owns a junior coaching record of 257-213-35.
In the NHL, Vigneault previously served as an assistant coach with the Ottawa Senators for the team's first three years -- under far less pressure than he will experience in hockey mad Montreal.
"I am very aware of the heritage and tradition that the Montreal Canadiens have," Vigneault said.
Vigneault played parts of two seasons as a defenceman for the St. Louis Blues in the early 1980s and got his first coaching experiece in 1986 at the junior level.
Tremblay replaced Jacques Demers as Montreal coach in October of 1995, and failed to win a playoff series in his two seasons with the Canadiens.
The Canadiens, the most successful team in the history of the NHL with 23 championships, have not won a playoff series since winning the Stanley Cup in 1993.
Montreal finished the 1996-97 campaign with a 31-36-15 record, claiming the the eighth and final playoff spot in the Eastern Conference.
The Canadiens lost in the first round of the playoffs to the New Jersey Devils four games to one.
